CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Social Community Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, Court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various regularly related parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from the message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 10

1. Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
2. Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency both for acts committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency and outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.
3. In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka for incidents committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER V

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 6

1. The Regional Government in organizing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:a. preventing acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; andc. providing assistance to victims.

CHAPTER VII

ORGANIZATION AND FORMS OF PROTECTION

Article 9

1. The Organization of Protection for victims is implemented in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
2. The PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection which in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the protection of Women and Children.
3. The organization of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must pay attention to religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The PPT is obliged to report in writing the implementation of the organization of protection for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.
2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; andd. performance.
3. Submission of reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 7

1. Social community organizations that participate in organizing protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

CHAPTER VIII

Article 12

1. The source of funds for organizing victim protection shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
2. In addition to the source of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), funds may come from other lawful sources.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Social Community Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, Court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various regularly related parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from the message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 14

Further provisions regarding technical implementation shall be regulated by Regent Regulation no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The PPT is obliged to report in writing the implementation of the organization of protection for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.
2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; andd. performance.
3. Submission of reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

CHAPTER VII

ORGANIZATION AND FORMS OF PROTECTION

Article 9

1. The Organization of Protection for victims is implemented in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
2. The PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection which in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the protection of Women and Children.
3. The organization of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must pay attention to religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 10

1. Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
2. Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency both for acts committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency and outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.
3. In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka for incidents committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER V

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 6

1. The Regional Government in organizing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:a. preventing acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; andc. providing assistance to victims.
